recognize_zh: 中央一顆漿細胞，細胞核被推到一側、染色質呈車輪狀，細胞質完全被大小不一的淡藍色圓形空泡樣小球（Russell bodies）塞滿，像一串葡萄，即 Mott 細胞（葡萄細胞）。
features: Plasma cell with an eccentric, compressed nucleus showing clumped chromatin
Cytoplasm packed with numerous round, pale blue, variably sized globules (Russell bodies) giving a grape-cluster appearance
Globules are homogeneous and non-refractile, consistent with condensed immunoglobulin
Adjacent granulocytic precursors (myelocyte/metamyelocyte) and a band neutrophil for comparison
Background red cells in a thick area of the aspirate
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a plasma cell with an eccentrically placed nucleus and cytoplasm distended by numerous round, pale blue, homogeneous globules of varying size, consistent with Russell bodies. Adjacent granulocytic precursors are present. Findings are consistent with a Mott cell. Mott cells reflect accumulation of immunoglobulin in dilated endoplasmic reticulum and are not specific for malignancy; in this patient they occur in the setting of multiple myeloma, and clonality should be established by light chain studies.

ddx.vs: Gaucher cells are large histiocytes with small nuclei and fibrillary crumpled tissue-paper cytoplasm rather than discrete round globules.
Dutcher bodies are intranuclear pseudoinclusions overlying the nucleus, whereas Russell bodies are cytoplasmic.
Burkitt cells have deeply basophilic cytoplasm with small clear lipid vacuoles and an immature nucleus rather than a mature plasma cell nucleus.
Foamy histiocytes have a central bland histiocytic nucleus and small uniform lipid vacuoles, without plasmacytoid features.
